# sddio

> sddio is a spec-driven development tool for coding agents. `SPEC`, `ADR` and `DISCUSSION` are plain Markdown files committed next to the code, so the reasoning behind a project survives session restarts and shows up in pull requests.

sddio is a Node CLI (`@sddio/cli`, MIT). `npx -y @sddio/cli@latest init` writes a package-owned context layer (`.sddio/`) and a user-owned workspace (`sddio_docs/`), appends a registration snippet to `AGENTS.md`, then prints one prompt to paste into a coding agent. It records decisions. It does not write code, index or search anything, send telemetry, require an account, or enforce its own rules.

## Canonical pages

- [README](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio#readme): positioning, quick start, how it compares with agent skills, Spec Kit and OpenSpec
- [FAQ](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/docs/faq.md): short, self-contained answers to the questions people actually ask, including the objections (skills overlap, AGENTS.md overlap, manual maintenance, context cost)
- [FAQ (中文速览)](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/docs/faq.zh-CN.md): the same questions condensed in Chinese
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/packages/cli/README.md): commands, flags, what lands in a project
- [SPEC](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/sddio_docs/spec/spec_100.md): the requirements this project holds itself to
- [ADR](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/sddio_docs/adr/adr_100.md): why it is built this way, including rejected options
- [DISCUSSION](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/sddio_docs/discussions/discussions_100.md): what is still unresolved
- [Distribution notes](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/docs/distribution.md): release and discoverability checklist
- [Migration to 0.4.0](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/docs/migrate-0.4.md): the procedure for a 0.3.x project whose block runs `npx sddio start`, which is a 404

## Facts

- License: MIT.
- Runtime: Node ≥ 18. No Python, no global install.
- Dependencies: none in the project. The CLI is fetched into npm's cache and pinned by the command in the `AGENTS.md` block; no devDependency, no lockfile. No runtime service, no daemon.
- Telemetry: none. No account, no server, no analytics, no update check.
- Execution: acts only when a caller declared in `.sddio/context/config.json` asks it to reconcile, or when a coding agent opens a session and reads `AGENTS.md`. No daemon, no scheduler.
- Updates: the `hooks` array in `config.json` records which caller is expected to trigger reconciliation and at which moment (`context.request`, `knowledge.reconcile`, `session.start`). A fresh project declares none (`hooks: []`); `flow-trail` is the only built-in one. No hook is required — without one the workspace simply goes stale until someone runs the check.
- Install: `init` asks which hook to use and installs the one chosen. `flow-trail` is chosen explicitly: its own bootstrap is fetched over the network, uses `git` to fetch a tag, and keeps a checkout in `~/.flow-trail`, then writes a card board into `flow-trail/`. Keeping the default (`none`) keeps everything inside the project.
- Non-destructive: `init` writes only missing files; an existing `AGENTS.md` is preserved and a delimited block carrying the pinned command is appended or updated in place. `--force` is the only path that replaces workspace files.
- Cross-agent: the workspace is the shared cache, not a memory inside one agent. No per-agent state — an entry written by one agent is read by the next, including a different model or a different tool, and the knowledge outlives the tool.
- Skills: complementary to agent skills, not a replacement. A skill supplies *how* to do the work and applies to every repository; sddio records *what this project already decided and why* and applies to one. Nothing is installed into an agent: `AGENTS.md` is the only integration point.
- Artifacts: `SPEC` (requirements), `ADR` (decisions), `DISCUSSION` (open questions) — plain Markdown, committed with the code. Work in progress is deliberately not an artifact; that belongs to a workflow tool.
- Upgrade behaviour: `.sddio/` is replaced in place, except the `hooks` declaration in `config.json`, which is preserved; `sddio_docs/` is never touched.
- Uninstall: delete `.sddio/` and the package; the workspace stays readable.
- Known limit: `check` compares the cursor with `HEAD` and names unrecorded files, but it cannot judge whether an entry still says the right thing — that stays the agent's reading.
- Agent support: any agent that reads repository files. Registration happens only through `AGENTS.md`; no agent configuration directory is written.

## One-line description for citation

sddio is a spec-driven development tool for coding agents: it keeps `SPEC`, `ADR` and `DISCUSSION` as plain Markdown in the repository, so the reasoning behind the code survives session restarts and is reviewable in a pull request.
